claims.text: The Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy is in a solid-solution state.
The dynamic response of Co-free FeNiCrMn arises from a temperature- and strain-rate-controlled transition between slow-avalanche and fast-runaway slip regimes.
Low temperature and high strain rate favor dominant dislocation pinning by solute atoms.
Solute pinning promotes work hardening and slow slip avalanches.
High temperature and low strain rate increase solute mobility and thereby weaken dislocation obstacles.
Dynamic weakening of dislocation obstacles triggers rapid, system-spanning runaway slip events.
Removing Co shifts FeNiCrMn toward greater dynamic weakening at high temperatures or low strain rates relative to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
Temperature and strain rate influence solute-dislocation interactions and the observed slip regime.
At low temperature and high strain rate, numerous small slip events enhance work hardening in Co-free FeNiCrMn.
At high temperature and low strain rate, reduced solute pinning permits rapid, large-scale slip events in Co-free FeNiCrMn.
The absence of Co increases the temperature sensitivity of solute-dislocation interaction energy.
Relative to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi, Co-free FeNiCrMn will show lower work-hardening and larger, more abrupt slip events under high-temperature or low-strain-rate conditions.
At low temperature and high strain rate, Co-free FeNiCrMn will maintain or improve work hardening relative to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi tested at identical temperatures and strain rates is the comparison baseline.
The proposed mechanism is restricted to the solid-solution regime in which dislocation-mediated plasticity dominates over creep and phase transformations.
The specific effect of removing Co on solute-dislocation interactions has not been fully characterized.
A temperature-by-strain-rate test matrix on both alloys, with high-resolution stress-strain and slip-event measurements, can distinguish the proposed regimes.

Failure of the Co-free alloy to show a statistically significant shift toward larger, faster slip events and reduced work hardening under high-temperature and low-strain-rate conditions would falsify the mechanism.
